ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two straight lines r and s slanting upward to the right, and they have the same pink arrow markings, indicating r ∥ s; a straight line q slanting downward to the right passes through r and s, serving as a transversal. At the upper intersection, ∠1 is located above line r and to the left of q, and ∠3 and ∠1 are vertical angles; at the lower intersection, ∠4 is located above line s and to the right of q. Reasoning: Because vertical angles are equal, m∠3 = m∠1 = 85. Also because r ∥ s, ∠3 and ∠4 are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary: m∠4 = 180 - 85 = 95. The problem gives m∠4 = 2x - 17, therefore 2x - 17 = 95, solving gives 2x = 112, x = 56.

Use vertical angles to get m∠3 = m∠1 = 85. Then use the parallel-line rule that same-side interior angles ∠3 and ∠4 are supplementary, so m∠4 = 180 - 85 = 95. From the text, m∠4 = 2x - 17, so solve 2x - 17 = 95 to get x = 56.
